skill.name: nano-image-generator
skill.description: Generate images with Gemini 3 Pro Preview using text prompts, aspect ratios, output sizes, and optional reference images.
skill.summary: Create visual assets through a local Python CLI backed by the Gemini image generation API.
skill.author: lxfater

security_audit.summary: The skill provides a legitimate Gemini-backed image generation workflow, but it has meaningful security concerns. The main confirmed issues are hardcoded API key setup, external transfer of prompts and reference images, local Python command execution, and unrestricted output-path writes. Documentation-only URLs, Markdown formatting, magic-byte checks, and response image base64 decoding were adjudicated as false positives.

remediation.issue: API key is configured by editing source code.
remediation.suggestion: Read the Gemini API key from an environment variable or a local secrets store, and remove documentation that asks users to hardcode real keys.

remediation.issue: API key is placed in the request URL query string.
remediation.suggestion: Use an authorization header or the safest authentication method supported by the API so credentials are less likely to appear in logs.

remediation.issue: Reference images and prompts are sent to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear disclosure before execution and warn users not to provide private images unless external processing is acceptable.
Resolve and validate output paths against an approved project directory before creating directories or writing files.

remediation.issue: Skill examples encourage automatic local command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact script behavior, required network access, and file writes so agents and users can request confirmation before running it.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded API Key Setup Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The README files and Python script instruct users to replace a source-code placeholder with a real Gemini API key. This creates a high chance of committing or sharing a live credential.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly says to replace the placeholder with an actual API key, and the script returns that literal value. This is direct evidence of unsafe credential storage by design.

semantic_findings.title: Reference Images Sent to External API
semantic_findings.description: The script reads each reference image, base64-encodes it, includes it in the request payload, and posts it to the Gemini API. Users may expose private images if they provide sensitive local files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code appends reference image bytes as inlineData and then sends the payload through urllib.request.urlopen. This is expected functionality, but it is a clear external data transfer.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Output Path Write
semantic_findings.description: The output path is provided by the caller, parent directories are created automatically, and image bytes are written to that path. A mistaken or manipulated path could overwrite files the process can access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly converts args.output into a Path, creates parent directories, and writes bytes. The forced image extension limits some abuse, but path scope is otherwise unrestricted.

content.value_statement: Teams need quick visual assets without leaving their coding workflow. This skill uses a local Python script to generate images with Gemini and save them into project folders.
actual_capabilities: Generates images from text prompts through Gemini 3 Pro Preview.
Supports square, portrait, landscape, mobile, and cinematic aspect ratios.
Accepts up to 14 reference images for style transfer or character consistency.
Writes generated images to a caller-selected local output path.
Detects returned image format and adjusts the saved file extension.
limitations: Requires a Gemini API key configured inside the Python script.
Sends prompts and reference images to the Google Gemini API.
Generated text and exact brand marks may be unreliable.
Requires local Python, network access, and write access to the output folder.

use_cases.title: Generate Product Graphics
use_cases.description: Create app icons, UI assets, and feature illustrations directly from project prompts.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Images
use_cases.description: Create banners, social images, and launch visuals with selected aspect ratios and sizes.

use_cases.title: Maintain Visual Consistency
use_cases.description: Use reference images to keep a consistent style or character across a sequence of assets.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple image from one description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an image of a friendly robot mascot waving, with a clean modern style, and save it to the generated folder.

prompt_templates.title: Sized Banner
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a marketing image with a specific layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 16:9 website hero banner for a productivity app with abstract geometric shapes and a calm professional color palette.

prompt_templates.title: Reference Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a source image to guide the visual style.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the reference image as the visual style and generate a new mountain scene with matching colors, lighting, and texture.

prompt_templates.title: Consistent Series
prompt_templates.scenario: Create several related assets with a shared look.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a three-image knowledge card series with a consistent layout, matching typography space, and a clear visual theme.

output_examples.input: Create a square app icon for a weather app with a simple cloud and sun symbol.
output_examples.output: A saved square image file suitable for an app icon draft, using the selected output folder.

output_examples.input: Create a wide launch banner for a developer tool in a clean editorial style.
output_examples.output: A landscape banner image with a generated file path returned after the script completes.

output_examples.input: Use this character reference and place the same character in a warm cafe scene.
output_examples.output: A new image that attempts to preserve the referenced character appearance in a different setting.

best_practices: Use specific prompts with subject, style, colors, composition, and intended use.
Store generated assets in project folders that match their purpose.
Review reference images before sending them to the external API.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real API keys in files committed to source control.
Do not send private reference images unless external processing is acceptable.
Do not rely on generated images for exact text, trademarks, or final brand approval.

faq.question: What model does this skill use?
faq.answer: It is designed for Gemini 3 Pro Preview image generation, described by the skill as Nano Banana Pro.

faq.question: Does it support reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts up to 14 reference images for style transfer or character consistency.

faq.question: Where are generated images saved?
faq.answer: The user provides an output path, and the script saves the returned image there with a detected extension.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends requests to the Google Generative Language API to generate images.

faq.question: How is the API key configured?
faq.answer: The current script asks users to place the Gemini API key inside the source file.

faq.question: Can it create exact text in images?
faq.answer: The skill notes that text rendering may be imperfect, so text overlays are better for final assets.
